children: Brent crude steadied above $97 per barrel on Thursday after rising in the previous session, as investors weighed signs of a recovery in Middle East flows against an ongoing impasse in US-Iran negotiations.

Crude shipments from the region were nearing pre-war levels after Saudi Arabia restored half the capacity of its East-West pipeline, while flows through the Strait of Hormuz climbed to 13.2 million barrels per day.

However, markets remain cautious about the durability of the recovery without a lasting agreement to end the Iran war, with both Tehran and Washington claiming full control over the strategic waterway.
Meanwhile, Iranian government spokesperson Fatemeh Mohajerani said Tehran had received a US proposal regarding the reopening of the strait.
Elsewhere, OPEC+ is expected to keep November output quotas unchanged at its meeting this weekend.

title: Brent Steadies as Middle East Uncertainty Persists
